//: rhizome-graph capture hooks. Copy the 'hooks' block into the OBSERVED
//instructions: project's .claude/settings.json. Adjust the absolute path to emit_event.py.
The hook only FORWARDS the raw PostToolUse JSON to the daemon over a Unix
socket; the daemon (daemon/server.py) normalizes it and owns the set of
already-seen paths that decides A (added) vs M (modified) for Write. That is
why there is no PreToolUse hook here: existence is tracked in the daemon, so
the first Write to a path is an add and any later Write is a modify, with no
filesystem probing on the hot path.
The hook is no longer the only source of events: the daemon also watches the
filesystem, so changes show up even without it. What the hook adds is WHO -
the agent id that puts a figure and a beam on the change. Note that Claude
Code reads settings.json at startup, so a session already open when you add
this block keeps running without it.
The matcher also covers Read, which is not a change to the tree at all: it
lights the file violet (R) while the agent is looking at it, so the graph
shows the reading that explains the edit instead of staying dark until the
edit lands. Reads are hook-only by nature - the filesystem watcher cannot see
them (atime is unreliable under relatime, and it does not subscribe to access
events), so without this block there is no read glow at all.
Env vars (optional): RHIZOME_SOCKET overrides the socket path and must
match the daemon; default is /tmp/rhizome-graph.sock. RHIZOME_DEBUG_LOG
names a file to append hook failures to - the only way to tell 'daemon down'
from 'nothing happened'. Prefix it on the command below to enable it.
